details:
I understand that for years the community was asking for the VRC Development team to implement some sort of system to prevent crashers / griefers. 
Everyone knew that mods were banned under the TOS. However, everyone also knew, that the enforcement system worked on a "don't ask, don't tell" policy. As long as you weren't utilizing mods for malicious reasons, you typically flew under the radar. 
I myself, never utilized mods, but there's no denying the community usage of them. 
I assume VRC Developers now had to spend valuable time and resources working on security solutions, rather than implementing new features in the game. 
I then assume they contacted third party agencies to see if they could provide this service, so they could work on much more valuable projects. 
Epic Games probably then came along and offered a fantastic deal from a busines perspective. 
Epic Games : "We already have a fantastic and proven EAC system that is implemented in a broad amount of games. we can provide the VRC Community network security services, and deal with your griefing issues. All moderation is handled in house here at Epic Games, so even if a end user has a complaint, we will accept all responsibility, as the EAC service provider. Now VRCHAT has less liability, and solves the issue it's community has been complaining about for years; and VRC devs can now focus on implementing features, rather than dealing with this issue. It's a win-win."
VRC : That sounds like a great idea, mods are already banned under our current TOS. Therefore any implementation will receive only minor backlash. If it's already banned even before we implement your security EAC services; they won't really have very much to complain about because there already not supposed to have it.
I assume VRC & Epic Games then entered into a MUTLI MILLION DOLLAR CONTRACT FOR LIKELY THE NEXT 5 YEARS. 
Now they quickly announce integration of this new contracted service. Expecting the community to have mixed, but overall mediocre responses. (Remember users are not supposed to have mods installed in the first place.) 
Now lets come back to the present. 
This was a foolish decision. 
First, who do you think pays for VRC subscriptions? Dedicated, and advanced users, the same people who utilize mods. 
Who do you think creates all the content inside of UNITY AND BLENDER, that's right the technically inclined advanced users, you don't think they use mods? 
With this EAC update VRC Developers have effectively targeted their only direct revenue stream.
How is this a smart business decision? 
I fully understand they likely already paid out a contract with Epic games to utilize their EAC services. 
I understand they can't just up and back out of the deal once they've already likely spent millions of dollars securing a deal.
Well, it's either take the L with Epic, or take the loss with the community which is your primary revenue source.
They chose the former, because I assume "they already spent the money."
(Epic Games is obviously not providing EAC services to VRCHAT for free.)
However, they can still save face, they have multiple ways in which they can do this:
They can simply hold off on implementing their contracted EAC services until they have the player requested solutions in hand to implement.
OR
They can officially support mods, to allow certain mods through EAC. 
They are bleeding capital right now, a lot of users honestly will not leave VRC, but they will absolutely reduce the production of content, and they will absolutely cancel their VRC Subscriptions. VRC has no other model of revenue generation, and they are not involved in the creation of content for obvious copyright avoidance reasons.  (If they did they would start to likely become responsible for all those copyrighted avatars.) 
Thus they have to remain a neutral platform. 
The only way they can make revenue is with advertisements, sponsored events, or VRC + Subscriptions. (Which I assume 90% is their primary method of revenue generation outside of capital investment groups.) 
VRC Development has no choice to be rationally look at this incident, and make a call one way or the other, doubling down at this point is financial suicide. 
Bite your pride VRC Development team, don't burn your entire monetary base because you already signed a deal with Epic Games. Just delay the implementation for the "foreseeable future" to save face; and your revenue stream.
title: EAC integration from a business standpoint.
